title: SAP BDC – Object Size Manager in Stories: Guided Path to a Leaner Story
author: thomas_fery
text:
"Your Story Is Too Large", But What Does That Mean? 
 SAP Analytics Cloud enforces size limits on stories. When a creator tries to save an asset that exceeds the threshold, a guardrail blocks the action. The intent is clear: oversized stories hurt performance, increase load times, and put unnecessary strain on the system. 
 The problem is what happens next. The creator sees the error, clicks through to the generic best practices documentation , and is left to figure out which objects are actually driving the size. There is no breakdown, no ranking, no clear starting point. Knowing a story is too large is not the same as knowing where to start fixing it. 
 What's New with Release 2026.20: Object Size Manager 
 The Object Size Manager is now available in the Info Panel of the Story Designer, the same panel that already surfaces Performance Recommendations and Consolidated Error Messages . One panel, all actionable design-time guidance. 
 You access it via the toolbar: Tools → Performance Optimization → Analyze Object Size . 

 What You See: A Full Breakdown of Your Story's Size Budget 
 Once the analysis completes, the Object Size tab opens in the Info Panel. The header immediately tells you where you stand: 
 Total Size: 5.22 MB of 90 MB limit 
 A visual bar shows the split between two categories: 
 Widgets: 3.82 MB (73%) — the pages and individual widgets in your story 
 Others: 1.40 MB (27%) — non-widget story objects: variables, global scripts, theme definitions, story metadata, configuration flags, and story-level constructs 

 The "Others" category deserves particular attention. It is easy to focus exclusively on charts and tables when hunting for size, but variables, global scripts, and theme definitions can quietly accumulate, especially in stories that have evolved over time. Hovering over the info icon next to "Others" surfaces the full explanation directly in the UI. 
 Drilling Into the Detail: Pages and Widgets 
 Below the summary bar, the table lists all objects across the story, in this example, 10 Pages and 427 Widgets . Each row shows the object name, its size in MB, its share of the total (%), and its type (Page, Chart, Story Popup, and so on). 
 Objects are sorted from largest to smallest, so the biggest offenders are always at the top. Pages can be expanded to reveal the individual widgets beneath them, allowing you to pinpoint exactly which chart, table, or popup is contributing most. 
 From the same table, the Action column lets you navigate directly to the object in the canvas, no manual searching required.

title: Um eventos que a gente não esquece #SITCWB2026
author: Marssel700
text:
No último dia 7 de novembro, aconteceu a quarta edição do SAP Inside Track Curitiba, o #SITCWB2026 . E já vou começar dizendo que foi um dos melhores eventos da SAP Community de que participei até hoje. Veja o Blog do evento . 
 E olha que não foram poucos! Já são 41 participações em SAP Inside Tracks e outros eventos da comunidade. Depois de tantos encontros, palestras, viagens e reencontros com amigos do ecossistema SAP, posso dizer que Curitiba conseguiu me surpreender. 

 Foi um sábado daqueles em que a gente chega cedo, encontra um monte de gente conhecida, conhece outras tantas pessoas e, quando percebe, o evento já está terminando. E ainda fica com aquela sensação de que poderia ter mais algumas horas de programação. 
 Curitiba, a terra das capivaras! 

 Não dá para falar do SAP Inside Track Curitiba sem mencionar a nossa querida capivara! 
 A capivara é um animal típico da América do Sul, muito presente no Brasil. Aqui em São Paulo, por exemplo, encontramos várias delas nas margens dos rios Pinheiros e Tietê. Mas Curitiba resolveu dar à capivara o reconhecimento que ela merece. 
 E a brincadeira acabou pegando! 
 A capivara virou praticamente uma mascote dos nossos SAP Inside Tracks pelo Brasil. Os bichinhos de pelúcia distribuídos nos sorteios já são uma atração à parte. Tem gente que acompanha o sorteio com mais expectativa do que resultado de certificação SAP! 

 Nesta edição, tivemos até uma capivara gigante circulando pelo evento, brincando com os participantes e posando para fotos. Foi uma atração divertida que ajudou a deixar o ambiente ainda mais descontraído. 
 E isso é algo de que gosto muito nos eventos da comunidade. Podemos falar de assuntos técnicos, arquitetura, desenvolvimento, inteligência artificial e projetos complexos, mas também precisamos ter momentos para conversar, rir e simplesmente aproveitar a companhia dos colegas. 
 Muito conteúdo SAP e, claro, muita inteligência artificial! 
 Se a capivara foi uma das estrelas da descontração, o SAP Joule foi uma das grandes estrelas do conteúdo técnico . 
 A inteligência artificial da SAP esteve presente em várias apresentações, mostrando como o ecossistema está evoluindo e como essas tecnologias estão começando a fazer parte do dia a dia dos profissionais. 
 E não estou falando apenas de apresentações conceituais. Tivemos demonstrações, experiências práticas, discussões sobre arquitetura, integração e possibilidades reais de utilização. 

 Uma das palestras foi a do Leandro Dante , que trouxe informações importantes sobre as diferentes modalidades de licenciamento e utilização do Joule. Um assunto muito relevante, principalmente porque, à medida que a tecnologia evolui, precisamos entender também como ela pode ser adotada pelas empresas. 
 Outro destaque foi a participação do Mustafa Bensan , que veio diretamente de Sydney, na Austrália! 
 O Mustafa conseguiu conciliar sua agenda profissional, que também envolve clientes no Brasil, para estar conosco em Curitiba. Sua apresentação mostrou possibilidades interessantes de interação com o Joule e outras tecnologias de inteligência artificial por meio de comandos de voz. 
 Foi muito bom acompanhar uma demonstração desse tipo e perceber o quanto ainda temos para explorar nessa área. 
 Também tivemos excelentes profissionais da própria região de Curitiba, como Cristiano Santos e Christian Geronasso , além de vários outros palestrantes que contribuíram para uma programação bastante diversificada. 
 O que mais gostei foi justamente essa combinação. Tivemos profissionais da SAP, desenvolvedores, arquitetos, consultores e especialistas compartilhando experiências sob diferentes perspectivas. 
 Afinal, um SAP Inside Track precisa ter espaço para quem trabalha com desenvolvimento, para quem atua nas áreas funcionais, para quem gerencia projetos e também para quem está buscando entender as próximas mudanças do mercado. 
 E Curitiba conseguiu reunir tudo isso. 
 Dá para maratonar o SITCWB2026 no YouTube! 

 Outra coisa que merece destaque foi a qualidade das gravações. 
 As apresentações foram registradas com uma produção muito boa, com imagem e áudio de qualidade profissional. Isso é especialmente importante porque o conhecimento compartilhado não precisa ficar restrito às pessoas que conseguiram participar presencialmente. 
 Recomendo que vocês acompanhem o canal SAP Inside Track Brasil no YouTube e procurem a playlist do SITCWB2026 . 
 Aliás, dá tranquilamente para separar algumas horas e fazer uma maratona do evento! 
 É uma excelente oportunidade para acompanhar o que profissionais experientes estão discutindo sobre SAP, inteligência artificial, desenvolvimento e transformação tecnológica. 
 E, para quem esteve no evento, também é uma forma de rever aquelas apresentações que chamaram mais atenção ou assistir às palestras que aconteceram simultaneamente em outro auditório. 
 Um evento que foi muito além das palestras 

 Outra coisa que me chamou a atenção foi o cuidado da organização com a experiência dos participantes. 
 Tivemos brincadeiras promovidas pelos patrocinadores, roda da fortuna, entrevistas, sorteios, espaços para conversar e, claro, nossa capivara gigante circulando pelo ambiente. 

 Essas atividades fizeram diferença. 
 O evento ficou leve, divertido e com bastante interação entre as pessoas. Não foi aquela programação em que todo mundo fica sentado o dia inteiro esperando a próxima apresentação. 
 Havia sempre alguma coisa acontecendo. 
 E os patrocinadores também tiveram a oportunidade de interagir com os participantes de uma maneira mais próxima, algo muito positivo para todos. 
 No final, o tempo passou tão rápido que fiquei pensando: será que um dia inteiro ainda é suficiente para um evento desse tamanho? 

 Será que Curitiba já merece um evento de dois ou três dias? 
 Essa foi uma reflexão que tive durante o SITCWB2026. 
 Com a quantidade de bons palestrantes, o interesse do público e a variedade de assuntos, acredito que Curitiba já tem espaço para pensar em novos formatos. 
 Quem sabe um evento de dois dias? Ou até três? 
 Outra possibilidade seria realizar encontros temáticos ao longo do ano, com uma edição mais técnica, outra dedicada à inteligência artificial, desenvolvimento, arquitetura ou soluções funcionais. 
 O próprio nome Inside Track combina com essa ideia de diferentes trilhas de conhecimento. 
 Poderíamos ter uma trilha para desenvolvedores, outra para consultores funcionais, uma voltada a SAP Business AI e assim por diante. 
 Essas trilhas poderiam acontecer simultaneamente, em diferentes auditórios, ou até em datas separadas. 
 Claro que organizar tudo isso exige tempo, voluntários, estrutura e patrocinadores. Quem já participou da organização de um SAP Inside Track sabe muito bem o trabalho que existe nos bastidores. 
 Mas, olhando para o que Curitiba conseguiu entregar, acredito que vale a pena começar essa conversa. 
 Quase 300 pessoas e uma comunidade cada vez mais forte  

 Outro ponto que merece reconhecimento foi a participação do público. 
 Tivemos quase 300 pessoas presentes , com um número de inscrições que, pelo que acompanhei, ultrapassou essa marca. 
 O mais interessante foi perceber a boa permanência das pessoas durante o evento. 
 Isso mostra que existe um público interessado em aprender, se atualizar e acompanhar as mudanças do mercado SAP. 
 E esse interesse não se limita aos profissionais que já possuem muitos anos de experiência. Os eventos da comunidade também são uma excelente oportunidade para quem está começando, buscando uma transição de carreira ou querendo conhecer novas tecnologias. 
 Curitiba tem uma comunidade muito ativa, com profissionais qualificados e uma vontade enorme de fazer acontecer. 
 Na minha opinião, o SITCWB2026 se colocou entre os grandes eventos SAP Community realizados no Brasil neste ano. E, considerando o nível de algumas apresentações e a presença de convidados internacionais, não fica devendo em conteúdo a muitos encontros que vemos pelo mundo. 
 Parabéns aos organizadores e voluntários! 
 Não poderia deixar de reconhecer quem tornou tudo isso possível. 
 Meus parabéns à Simone, Adriano, Luiz Carlos de Souza e a toda a equipe de organização da SAP Community Curitiba. 
 E aqui faço questão de destacar os voluntários. 
 Muitas vezes, quem participa de um evento não imagina quantas reuniões, mensagens, ajustes de agenda, contatos com patrocinadores, preparação de salas e imprevistos existem até que tudo esteja pronto. 
 Tudo isso é feito por pessoas que dedicam parte do próprio tempo para proporcionar oportunidades de aprendizado e networking aos demais profissionais. 
 E o resultado estava ali, diante de todos nós. 
 Um evento muito bem organizado, com excelente conteúdo e um ambiente que realmente representou o espírito da SAP Community. 
 Que venham os próximos SAP Inside Tracks! 
 Saí de Curitiba com aquela sensação boa de ter participado de algo que realmente valeu a pena. 
 Depois de tantos anos frequentando e ajudando a organizar eventos da SAP Community, continuo acreditando muito nesse modelo de compartilhamento de conhecimento. 
 É impressionante o que um grupo de profissionais voluntários consegue realizar quando decide trabalhar junto. 
 O SAP Inside Track Curitiba 2026 foi mais uma demonstração disso. 
 Meu agradecimento a todos os organizadores, voluntários, patrocinadores, palestrantes e participantes que fizeram parte desse encontro. 
 Parabéns, SAP Community Curitiba! Vocês entregaram um evento espetacular. 
 Espero voltar nas próximas edições e encontrar ainda mais profissionais participando dessa comunidade. 
 E, para quem ainda não conhece um SAP Inside Track, fica o convite: procure o próximo evento, reserve um espaço na agenda e participe. Quem sabe, na próxima edição, você também não estará no palco compartilhando suas experiências? 

 Marssel Vilaça

title: How We Built a Mass Hiring and Data Management Solution for SAP SuccessFactors HCM Using SAP BTP
author: KavyaManohara
text:
Introduction 
 Managing workforce data efficiently is one of the biggest operational challenges for organizations using SAP SuccessFactors HCM. As organizations grow, HR teams must handle increasing volumes of employee records, organizational data, foundation objects, contingent workers, and hiring activities. 
 These operations often involve navigating multiple SuccessFactors screens, performing repetitive data entry, maintaining dependencies between different entities, and validating records individually. During high-volume recruitment drives, seasonal hiring, or organizational restructuring, these activities can become particularly time-consuming. 
 From bulk employee hiring and onboarding to foundation data maintenance and contingent workforce management, HR administrators need a reliable way to perform these operations without compromising data accuracy or governance. 
 This led us to build a Mass Hiring and Data Management Solution for SAP SuccessFactors HCM , powered by SAP Business Technology Platform (BTP). 
 Our goal was to bring multiple workforce data management capabilities into one centralized application, helping organizations simplify HR operations, accelerate hiring, and maintain consistent data across their SAP SuccessFactors landscape. 
 The Challenges We Wanted to Address 
 While working with SAP SuccessFactors environments, we identified several recurring challenges in managing large volumes of workforce data. 
 Some of the most common difficulties include: 

 Repetitive manual operations: HR administrators spend considerable time entering, updating, and maintaining employee and organizational records individually. 

 Delays in high-volume recruitment: Hiring large numbers of employees and contingent workers can become difficult when processes depend on individual record creation. 

 Data inconsistencies: Maintaining relationships between positions, departments, job classifications, business units, and cost centers requires careful coordination. 

 Duplicate employee records: Rehiring former employees without proper identification can result in duplicate records and incorrect employment history. 

 Complex contingent workforce management: Updating work orders, extending contracts, and transferring contingent workers often involves multiple administrative steps. 

 Limited bulk administration capabilities: Creating, inactivating, deleting, and copying foundation data across SuccessFactors instances can require significant manual effort. 

 Lack of centralized monitoring: HR teams need better visibility into bulk operations, validation errors, successful updates, and failed records. 
 We wanted to address these challenges through a unified solution that reduces manual intervention while maintaining data accuracy, security, and traceability. 
 Our Solution 
 We developed the Mass Hiring and Data Management Solution for SAP SuccessFactors HCM on SAP Business Technology Platform (BTP). 
 The solution brings multiple SuccessFactors data management and workforce administration capabilities together in a modern SAP Fiori application. 
 Instead of switching between different screens and performing repetitive operations, users can manage bulk data operations from a centralized interface. 
 The application supports: 

 Bulk import and export of SuccessFactors data. 

 Creation, modification, inactivation, and deletion of foundation data. 

 Mass hiring of regular employees and contingent workers. 

 Bulk onboarding initiation. 

 Automatic identification of former employees for rehire processing. 

 Organizational data synchronization and mass position changes. 

 Bulk employee changes, including termination, compensation, leave, and HRBP updates. 

 Contingent worker contract and work order management. 

 Data copying between multiple SuccessFactors instances. 

 Execution monitoring with downloadable success and error logs. 
 The solution connects securely to SAP SuccessFactors through OData APIs and can be accessed as a standalone application or integrated into SAP Build Work Zone. 
 One of our key design principles was to ensure that every bulk operation is validated before submission and that its execution results are recorded for transparency and troubleshooting. This enables organizations to perform large-scale data operations through a controlled and auditable application environment. 
 Key Features and Benefits 
 The application provides five major functional areas through its home dashboard. 
 1. Import and Export Data Management 
 Managing large volumes of SuccessFactors data often requires repeated uploads and downloads across different entities. 
 We brought these capabilities together into one centralized data management area. 
 Key capabilities include: 

 Refresh Metadata: Retrieves the latest entity and field definitions from SuccessFactors to ensure templates and validations reflect the current configuration. 

 Download Template: Generates SuccessFactors-aligned templates with the relevant columns and mandatory fields for supported entities. These templates can also be shared with recruitment partners and agencies. 

 Import Data: Supports bulk data loading for entities such as Biographical Information, Employment Details, Job History, Pay Range, and Compensation Information. 

 Flexible Import Modes: Users can choose between Incremental Load and Full Purge, depending on their data management requirements. 

 Scheduled Import: Supports immediate execution as well as scheduled data import jobs. 

 Export Data: Extracts SuccessFactors records on demand or through scheduled jobs. 

 Future-Dated Records: Provides visibility into records that have been loaded but are not yet effective. 
 These capabilities reduce repetitive data handling and provide a consistent approach to importing and exporting SuccessFactors information. 
 2. Data Administration 
 Foundation data is essential for maintaining organizational structures and ensuring consistency across Employee Central. 
 However, creating and maintaining foundation objects individually can become difficult when organizations manage large and frequently changing datasets. 
 Our Data Administration module simplifies these activities. 
 Key capabilities include: 

 Create Data: Create foundation objects such as Position, Business Unit, Cost Center, Department, and Location, along with supported employee data. 

 Inactivate Records: Identify and deactivate obsolete records in bulk. 

 Delete Records: Search and select multiple records for bulk deletion. 

 Copy Data: Copy supported foundation and employee data between different SuccessFactors instances. 
 For example, organizations can copy foundation data from a production environment to a test environment, significantly reducing the effort required to prepare test systems. 
 3. Rapid Mass Hiring and Initiate Onboarding 
 High-volume recruitment is one of the areas where manual HR administration can create significant delays. 
 Whether an organization is conducting graduate recruitment, seasonal hiring, or a large workforce expansion, creating employee records individually can consume considerable time. 
 Our Mass Hiring module simplifies this process by allowing HR teams to hire multiple employees and contingent workers through a single application. 
 Key capabilities include: 
 Mass Employee Hiring 
 Create multiple employee records in Employee Central through a single operation using uploaded files or the application interface. 
 Mass Onboarding Initiation 
 Import pre-hire records and initiate onboarding for multiple candidates at once, reducing repetitive administrative activities. 
 Mass Contingent Hiring 
 Manage contingent worker hiring alongside regular employee hiring through the same validated process. 
 Automatic Rehire Detection 
 One important capability is the automatic identification of former employees. 
 Before creating a new employee record, the solution checks attributes such as First Name, Last Name, Date of Birth, National ID, and other relevant information. 
 When an existing inactive employee record is identified, the appropriate rehire process is applied instead of creating an unnecessary duplicate. 
 Pre-Submission Validation 
 The application validates mandatory fields, data formats, and applicable business rules before submitting records to SuccessFactors. 
 Errors are highlighted at both row and field levels, helping users identify and correct issues before processing. 
 Execution Logs and Dashboards 
 Every hiring request is tracked through an execution dashboard. 
 Users can monitor: 

 Total records processed. 

 Successful records. 

 Failed records. 

 Detailed error information. 

 Downloadable success and error reports. 
 Failed records can be corrected and resubmitted, making the hiring process easier to monitor and manage. 
 4. Organizational Data Synchronization and Mass Employee Changes 
 Organizational data must remain consistent across different SuccessFactors entities to support accurate workforce administration and reporting. 
 Our solution provides synchronization capabilities and bulk employee change operations to simplify these activities. 
 Organizational Data Synchronization 
 The application helps identify and align relationships such as: 

 Job Classification to Position. 

 Department to Position Cost Center. 
 It supports mismatch detection, delta synchronization, and job schedule monitoring. 
 This helps organizations identify inconsistencies and maintain better alignment between organizational structures. 
 Mass Position Changes and Job Relationships 
 HR administrators can update position attributes and maintain matrix manager relationships in bulk instead of modifying each record individually. 
 Bulk Workforce Changes 
 The solution also provides centralized capabilities for several employee administration activities, including: 

 Mass Terminations. 

 Mass Pay Changes. 

 Mass Pay Range Updates. 

 Mass Leave of Absence. 

 HRBP Changes. 

 Probation Status Updates. 

 Mass Onboarding Cancellation. 
 These capabilities help reduce repetitive administrative work and simplify large-scale workforce changes. 
 5. Contingent Data Management 
 Managing contingent workers requires maintaining accurate contract details, work orders, vendor information, and organizational assignments. 
 Our Contingent Data Management module brings these activities into one place. 
 Key capabilities include: 
 Edit Work Orders - Update billing amounts, rates, currencies, and vendor details for individual or multiple contingent workers. 
 Update Contracts - Extend or end multiple contingent worker contracts through a single operation. 
 Transfer Contracts - Manage contract transfers while maintaining the required workforce information. 
 Assign Positions - Update position assignments and reporting relationships without manually navigating multiple SuccessFactors screens. 
 By bringing these capabilities together, the solution simplifies contingent workforce administration and helps HR teams manage contract-related changes more efficiently. 
 Business Value 
 The Mass Hiring and Data Management Solution delivers value across multiple HR operational areas. 
 1. Reduced Manual Effort 
 Bulk operations replace repetitive record-by-record updates, allowing HR administrators to focus on more strategic workforce activities.

 What kind of skill is this? What should the output look like? What happens when the data source returns nothing? Where do the rules go?

title: Export Query Results from Data Explorer in SAP SPM Data Manager Self-Service
author: Chaitanya444
text:
Introduction 
 In SAP Sales Performance Management (SAP SPM / SAP Incentive Management), the Data Explorer in Data Manager Self-Service lets you browse the database schemas and run read-only SQL queries directly from the UI. Until now, the results could only be viewed on screen. A recent enhancement adds an Export As option, so query results can be downloaded as a .csv or .xlsx file. In this blog post, I explain where to find Data Explorer, what it offers, how to use the new export option step by step, and a few practical scenarios where it saves time. 
 Data Explorer at a glance 
 Open Data Manager Self-Service from the app menu, then select Data Explorer (the console icon) in the left navigation. The screen has two main areas. 

 Screenshot: Data Explorer overview 
 Database Schemas panel 
 On the left, the Database Schemas panel lets you browse schemas, tables and columns. It shows the schemas available to you, such as EXT for custom extension objects and TCMP for the standard SPM tables, each with its number of objects. A search box helps you find a table or column quickly without remembering its exact name. 
 SQL Query Viewer (Read-Only) 
 On the right, the SQL Query Viewer is a read-only SQL interface for data verification. You type a SELECT statement and click Run Query , or press Cmd/Ctrl + Enter . For example: 
 SELECT NAME, EFFECTIVESTARTDATE, EFFECTIVEENDDATE
 FROM TCMP.CS_POSITION
 WHERE REMOVEDATE = TO_DATE('2200-01-01'); 
 The results appear in a grid below the editor, with the row count shown in the header, for example Results (1000) . 
 Built-in guardrails 
 The tool shows its rules in an information box above the editor: 
 RuleWhat it means for you 

 Read-only 
 Editing or modifying data is disabled. Only queries that read data can be run. 

 No LIMIT or OFFSET 
 Pagination is handled automatically, so leave these clauses out. 

 30-second timeout 
 Long-running queries are stopped to protect system performance. Filter and select only the columns you need. 

 Audit logging 
 Every query is logged with your user ID and a timestamp for compliance. 
 What's new: Export As 
 Previously, query results could only be read on screen. To share or analyse them further, you had to copy rows manually or ask someone with backend access to extract the data. The new Export As button in the top-right corner of the results grid removes that step. It offers two formats: 
 FormatBest for 

 .csv 
 Feeding results into other tools, scripts or comparison utilities; plain text and lightweight 

 .xlsx 
 Sharing with business users and quick analysis in Excel with filters, pivots and formatting 
 How to export query results 
 Open Data Manager Self-Service and select Data Explorer . 
 Find the table you need in the Database Schemas panel, or search for it by name. 
 Write your SELECT statement in the SQL Query Viewer . 
 Click Run Query , or press Cmd/Ctrl + Enter , and check the results in the grid. 
 Click Export As above the results grid. 
 Choose .csv or .xlsx . The file downloads to your machine. 
 Note: The export currently includes a maximum of 1,000 rows , the same as the results grid. If your query returns more, see the tips under Things to keep in mind for exporting larger result sets in batches. 

 Screenshot: Export As menu with .csv and .xlsx options 
 Practical use cases 
 From a data integration point of view, these are the scenarios where the export option helps most: 
 Validating data loads. After an inbound load, export the staged or promoted records and compare them with the source file to confirm counts and values. 
 Reviewing custom procedure logs. Many implementations write step-by-step debug messages from custom stored procedures into a log table in the EXT schema. Exporting those logs makes it easy to trace a run, filter by connection or run ID, and attach the evidence to a defect. 
 Sharing data with business users. Give business users an .xlsx extract of positions, participants or territories they can filter and review themselves, without needing database access. 
 Reconciliation and audits. Export snapshots before and after a change to compare them side by side, for example during cutover or testing. 
 Supporting defect analysis. Attach the exact query and its exported result to a ticket so others can reproduce the issue. 
 Things to keep in mind 
 Export is limited to 1,000 rows. When the results header shows 1000+ , the file contains only the first 1,000 rows. Run a SELECT COUNT(*) with the same WHERE clause first, so you know whether you need more than one export. 
 Export larger result sets in batches. Split the data with filters that each return fewer than 1,000 rows, such as a date range, a business unit or a range of IDs. Because LIMIT and OFFSET are not allowed, you can number the rows with ROW_NUMBER() and filter on that number instead. Always order by a unique column so each batch is consistent: 
 SELECT *
 FROM (SELECT p.NAME, p.EFFECTIVESTARTDATE, p.EFFECTIVEENDDATE,
 ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY p.NAME, p.EFFECTIVESTARTDATE) AS RN
 FROM TCMP.CS_POSITION p
 WHERE p.REMOVEDATE = TO_DATE('2200-01-01'))
 WHERE RN BETWEEN 1001 AND 2000; 
 Use the right tool for full extracts. For large or recurring extracts, use your standard outbound or extract process rather than many manual batches. 
 Keep queries efficient. The 30-second timeout applies to the query, so filter with a WHERE clause and select only the columns you need before exporting. 
 Handle exported data carefully. Files leave the system once downloaded. Compensation, participant and customer data can be sensitive, so follow your organisation's data-protection rules for storing and sharing them. 
 Remember the audit trail. Every query is logged with your user ID and timestamp, so use the tool for genuine verification and support tasks. 
 It is still read-only. Export is for getting data out. To change data, use the standard import and integration processes. 
 Conclusion 
 In this blog post, we looked at Data Explorer in SAP SPM Data Manager Self-Service: the schema browser, the read-only SQL Query Viewer and its built-in guardrails. You learned how the new Export As option turns query results into .csv or .xlsx files in a few clicks, and where it helps most, from validating data loads and reviewing logs to sharing extracts with business users. Together, querying and exporting in one place make day-to-day data verification faster and reduce the need for backend access.

title: Know Your Groups and How They Land in the Identity Directory
author: ivelinakiryakov
text:
Once multiple applications start provisioning groups into the Identity Directory, administrators face a common challenge: How do you tell where groups come from? SAP Cloud Identity Services provide two mechanisms to address this challenge: group prefixes and application IDs . While both help identify the source of a group, they serve different purposes. 
 In November 2026, SAP Cloud Identity Services introduced the application-level group prefix. Prefixes can now be configured directly on an application in the SCI administration console, in addition to being defined on the provisioning system. This is primarily intended for SAP-managed provisioning scenarios, where the provisioning system configuration is not visible to administrators. 
 While the new feature gives administrators more flexibility where prefixes are configured, it also raises the question: When should you use a prefix, when should you use application ID, and when should you use both? 
 Two mechanisms. Multiple configuration points. Similar goals, but different outcomes. 
 Let's look at how they differ and how to choose the right approach. 
 To illustrate the differences, we'll start with two source systems, each configured to provision one group to the Identity Directory: 
 SAP Integrated Business Planning (IBP): IPS_TEST_ROLE_1 
 SAP Field Service Management (FSM): Test_Group__SECOND-COMPANY 

 The Starting Point: No Distinction 

 In this case, no special configuration is applied. Neither group prefixes nor application IDs are configured in the provisioning systems using the corresponding properties: 
 fsm.group.prefix=<prefix> and ibp.group.prefix=<prefix> 
 ips.application.id=<application_ID>. 
 As expected, both groups arrive in the Identity Directory with their original display names. Nothing in the group name indicates whether it comes from FSM or IBP. 

 The Classic Approach: Group Prefixes Group prefixes are the simplest way to make the source of provisioned groups immediately visible. They can be configured either on the provisioning system or the application. 
 On the provisioning system (Properties tab) 
 This option is intended for customer-managed provisioning scenarios. In the following example, the properties are configured for the FSM and IBP source systems: 
 fsm.group.prefix=FSM_ 
 ibp.group.prefix=IBP_ 
 Following a provisioning job, the result is straightforward. The origin of each group can be easily identified by its prefix. 

 On the application (Provisioning tab) 
 This option is introduced primarily for customers using SAP-managed provisioning, where the provisioning systems are configured and maintained by SAP and are not visible in the administration UI. 
 In this scenario, administrators cannot configure a prefix through the provisioning system's Properties tab. Instead, the Group Prefix field under Applications & Resources → [Your Application] → Provisioning provides an alternative way to control group display names. 

 If a group prefix is configured at both levels, the application-level prefix takes priority. 
 In the example below, the provisioning system uses FSM_ , but the provisioned group receives FSM_DEV_ from the application. 

 The new feature is not limited to SAP-managed provisioning. Customers using customer-managed provisioning can also configure the group prefix from the application. For this to work, the application ID must be set for the ips.application.id property on the provisioning system from which groups are read, and a read job must be run on that system after the application-level prefix is configured. 
 Setting the application ID property actually turns the groups into application-specific groups. For more information, see The Modern Approach section below. 
 Use group prefixes when visibility is your primary goal. They can also control which groups are provisioned to a target system. If a prefix is configured on the target, only groups with that prefix are provisioned. 

 The Modern Approach: Application-Specific Groups 

 Instead of relying on a naming convention, this approach links groups directly to their source application by attaching the application ID as a group attribute. 
 When the ips.application.id property is configured on a source system, every provisioned group is associated with the ID of the corresponding application. In the Identity Directory, this association is resolved to the application name and displayed in the Application column under Users & Authorizations → Groups . 

 The biggest advantage of this approach is the event-driven provisioning. Once groups are associated with an application, changes to their membership or attributes automatically trigger provisioning to target systems, provided that Central Store-Based Provisioning is enabled for the application. No manual execution or scheduled provisioning job is required. 
 In our test scenario, ips.application.id was configured along with the existing prefixes. The groups retain their prefix and are linked to the application. 

 Use application-specific groups when automation and real-time provisioning is your primary goal. Group prefixes have no event-driven capabilities and provisioning only happens when a job runs. 

 Know the Name. Know the Source. Know the Behavior. 

 So, when the next hundred groups land in your Identity Directory, you won't just know their names. You'll know where they come from, how they are managed, and how they move across your landscape. 
 A simple rule of thumb: Use group prefixes for visibility. Use application-specific groups for automation. Use both when you want the best of both worlds.

title: Is It Possible to Change the First and Last Name of an SAP S-user ID?
author: monikar03
text:
Is It Possible to Change the First and Last Name of an SAP S-user ID? 

 Have you ever wondered whether you could change the first name or last name associated with your SAP S-user ID? Perhaps you noticed a spelling mistake during registration, entered your first and last names in the wrong fields, or recently changed your legal name. 
 Whatever the reason, it is important to understand how SAP handles S-user identity information and what steps you need to follow to request a correction. 
 The short answer is yes, SAP can update the name associated with an S-user ID in certain circumstances, but you cannot make this change yourself through the usual profile settings. You must contact SAP and provide a valid reason for the requested correction. 
 Let's explore the details, the situations in which SAP permits name changes, and how you can submit your request. 
 Why Can't You Change Your Name Directly in an SAP S-User ID? 
 An SAP S-user ID is intended for use by one specific individual. It is associated with a history of activities and records, including authorizations, cases, service requests, certifications, and other SAP-related interactions. 
 Because this information is linked to an individual's identity, SAP does not allow an S-user ID to be reused, transferred, or overwritten for another person. 
 For the same reason, SAP restricts changes to the first and last names associated with an S-user ID. These restrictions help maintain the integrity of user records and prevent an existing account from being passed on to another individual. 
 The email address associated with the S-user should also correspond to the user's first and last name, helping ensure that the account remains associated with the correct person. 
 Although certain contact details can be updated, name changes require SAP's involvement. Depending on the information being changed, some updates may also need to be performed by an administrator. For more information, refer to SAP Note 1271545 . 

 Under What Circumstances Can SAP Change an S-User's Name? 
 SAP may approve a name correction when the S-user ID continues to belong to the same individual and there is a legitimate reason for the change. 
 The following situations are generally accepted: 
 Incorrect Spelling of the Name 
 If your first name or last name was entered incorrectly during registration, you can request a correction. 
 For example, if your name is Michael Johnson but your S-user profile displays Micheal Johnson , you can contact SAP to request the spelling correction. 
 First Name and Last Name Entered in the Wrong Fields 
 Sometimes, the first name and surname are accidentally entered in the wrong fields. 
 For example, your actual name is David Miller , but your profile displays Miller David . In this situation, you can request that SAP correct the name fields. 
 Incorrect Capitalization of the First Letter 
 If the first letter of your name was mistakenly entered in lowercase, you can request a correction. 
 For instance, if your name appears as john smith instead of John Smith , SAP can review the request to correct the capitalization. 
 Legal Name Change 
 If your legal name has changed, you can request an update to your S-user ID. 
 Common examples include a name change following marriage, a change in marital status, or a legal name change associated with a gender transition. 
 Important: These exceptions apply only when the S-user ID belongs to the same individual. SAP will not approve a name change intended to transfer an existing S-user ID to another person or replace the original user's identity with an alias. 

 How to Request a First Name or Last Name Change for an SAP S-User ID 
 If your situation falls under one of the accepted reasons, follow the process below to request a correction. 
 Step 1: Contact SAP or Your S-User Administrator 
 You can initiate the request yourself as the owner of the S-user ID or ask your S-user administrator to submit it on your behalf. 
 Step 2: Create a Case Using Component XX-SER-FORME 
 Create a case with SAP using component XX-SER-FORME , following the guidance in SAP KBA   1296527 . 
 Clearly explain that you need to correct the first name or last name associated with your existing S-user ID. 
 Step 3: Provide the Required Information 
 Include the following details in your request: 
 S-user ID: The identifier associated with your account. 
 Current name: The first name and last name currently displayed on the S-user ID. 
 Requested name: The corrected first name and last name. 
 Reason for the change: Briefly explain why the correction is necessary. 
 Providing complete and accurate information helps SAP understand the purpose of the request and determine whether the change is appropriate. 
 Alternatively, you can send a written request to t he Customer Int eraction Center from the email address associated with the S-user ID, along with the reason for the name change as listed above, where applicable. Your request should clearly identify the S-user ID and explain the requested correction. 
 Step 4: Wait for SAP's Review 
 Once the necessary details have been submitted, the request will be forwarded to SAP's internal team for review and processing. 
 The team will assess the information and determine whether the requested change meets SAP's requirements. 
 Step 5: Receive Confirmation 
 After the request has been processed, SAP will notify you by email or update the support case with the outcome. 
 If additional information is needed, you may be asked to provide clarification or supporting documents before the request can be completed. 
 What If You Want to Change the Name Because Another Person Will Use the S-User ID? 
 This is an important distinction. 
 Suppose an employee leaves your organization and another employee needs access to SAP support services. You might consider changing the first and last names on the existing S-user ID so the new employee can use it. 
 SAP does not permit this. 
 An S-user ID is assigned to an individual, and its associated history must remain connected to that person. Changing the name to another person's identity would undermine this principle. 
 If the requested change is intended to allow another person to use the account, SAP will advise you to create a new S-user ID instead. 
 For instructions, refer to SAP Note 1271482 . 
 Creating a separate S-user ID ensures that the new user has an individual identity and that their authorizations, incidents, service messages, certifications, and other activities are associated with the correct person. 
 Will Changing Your Name in SAP Cloud Identity Update Your S-User ID? 
 No. This is a common point of confusion. 
 You may be able to update your personal information through the SAP Cloud Identity (SAP ID Service) profile management page: 
 https://accounts.sap.com/ui/protected/profilemanagement 
 However, changing your personal information on this page does not update the official first name or last name associated with your S-user ID. 
 Changes made there affect the display or vanity name shown on other SAP sites and services, such as SAP Community and Jam, rather than the official identity information maintained for your S-user ID. 
 If you need to correct the official name associated with your S-user ID, you must follow the SAP support process described above. 

 By following the appropriate process and providing the necessary information, you can help SAP review and resolve your name correction request smoothly. 
 Useful SAP Knowledge Base Articles: 
 1271545 : Information about changes to S-user details and administrator permissions. 
 2597456 : Guidance for requesting an S-user name correction. 
 1271482 : Guidance on creating a new S-user ID.

title: Look who's calling. How to identify client in Integration Cell API
author: jirifridrich
text:
One API artifact on Integration Cell, several external partners, one URL, and each partner may see only its own data. Sounds simple, until you try to find out who is actually calling. 
 With Basic authentication (or the default XSUAA tokens) it doesn’t work: service keys share the same client ID, and the API artifact even swaps the authenticated user for the destination user before your logic runs. With external OAuth through SAP IAS, the token reaches the artifact as-is, and one claim tells you exactly which partner is on the other side. 
 In this post I show why, how to set up IAS and the API artifact in a few steps, and what to do when a partner can’t use OAuth.

title: Advanced Intercompany Sales no Brasil: como localizar o processo no SAP S/4HANA
author: ThalesMacedo
text:
Advanced Intercompany Sales no Brasil: como localizar o processo no SAP S/4HANA 
 Quando trabalhei pela primeira vez com o processo de Advanced Intercompany Sales no SAP S/4HANA, o que chamou atenção imediatamente foi o monitor integrado — ele mostra exatamente onde o fluxo está e por que ele pode ter parado. Para quem já enfrentou a dificuldade de rastrear processos intercompany em ambientes complexos, isso representa um avanço concreto. 
 O Advanced Intercompany Sales é uma opção robusta para empresas que precisam de um processo intercompany automatizado, com rastreabilidade nativa e menos dependência de intervenções manuais. Para empresas brasileiras, porém, há um passo adicional indispensável: a localização fiscal. Neste post, vou compartilhar o que foi necessário fazer para localizar o processo para o Brasil — das configurações padrão no customizing até os desenvolvimentos customizados para emissão correta da Nota Fiscal Eletrônica (NF-e). 
 Pré-requisito: ativando a solução. 
 Antes de qualquer configuração, é preciso garantir que a solução esteja ativa no sistema. As referências abaixo cobrem os passos de ativação e as restrições por versão: 
 SAP Note 3233830 — Configuration Steps for Advanced Intercompany Sales in SAP S/4HANA 
 Scope Item 5D2 — Advanced Intercompany Sales 
 SAP Note 3366067 — SAP S/4HANA 2023: Restrictions and General Information for Advanced Intercompany Sales 
 SAP Note 3672804 — SAP S/4HANA 2025 FPS01/FPS02: Restrictions and General Information for Multistage Intercompany Sales 
 Recomendo verificar cada nota com atenção antes de prosseguir, pois as restrições variam conforme o release utilizado. 
 Configurações fiscais padrão para NF-e 
 Com a solução ativa, o próximo passo é configurar o processo de vendas para emissão de NF-e. O Carminho no customizing é: 
 SAP Customizing Implementation Guide → Sales and Distribution → Billing → Billing Documents → Country/Region-Specific Features → Country-specific Features for Brazil 
 Três configurações são obrigatórias: 
 Assign Nota Fiscal Type to Sales Document Types — associa o tipo de NF-e ao tipo de ordem de vendas. 
 Maintain Sales Document Item Category — ativa as categorias de item de ordem de venda para emissão de NF-e. 
 Maintain Billing Document Item Category — ativa as categorias de item de faturamento para emissão de NF-e. 
 Sem essas configurações, o processo não consegue gerar a NF-e corretamente. 
 O desafio da planta intercompany é a filial emissora da NF-e. 
 Aqui começa o ponto mais crítico da localização. No Advanced Intercompany Sales, o item da Ordem de Vendas tem uma planta atribuída a de uma empresa diferente da empresa vendedora. Isso cria dois problemas para a emissão da NF-e. 
 O primeiro: a filial (campo BUPLA) e a planta (campo WERKS) no faturamento precisam refletir a empresa que está emitindo a nota. O segundo: os dados do parceiro de negócios destinatário precisam ser transferidos corretamente para a NF-e. Ambos os problemas exigem desenvolvimento customizado. 
 Desenvolvimento 1: ajuste dos campos BUPLA e WERKS via VOFM. 
 O primeiro desenvolvimento corrige os campos BUPLA e WERKS no faturamento do cliente. Para isso, utilizamos a transação VOFM, que gerencia as fórmulas de controle de cópia no SAP S/4HANA. 

 A abordagem adotada na nossa Prova de Conceito (PoC) foi criar um enhancement na fórmula utilizada no controle de cópia da remessa para o faturamento do cliente. O enhancement garante o preenchimento correto dos campos antes de o documento de faturamento ser salvo. Uma alternativa igualmente válida é criar uma fórmula por cópia. A escolha entre as duas abordagens deve considerar as práticas de extensibilidade do projeto e as diretrizes de Clean Core aplicáveis ao ambiente. 

 Desenvolvimento 2: ajuste do parceiro de negócios via USER-EXIT. 
 O segundo desenvolvimento trata da substituição do parceiro de negócios na NF-e. No contexto intercompany, o parceiro WE (destinatário da entrega) pode não corresponder ao parceiro correto para emissão da nota fiscal. 
 A solução adotada foi utilizar a seguinte USER-EXIT: 
 RV60AFZD — Form USEREXIT_NEWROLE_XVBPAP_AVBPAK 
 Nela, substituímos os dados do parceiro WE usando como referência o parceiro RE (destinatário da fatura). Com esse ajuste, a NF-e passa a ser emitida para o destinatário correto. 

 Considerações finais: PoC, Clean Core e próximos passos. 
 Todo o processo descrito aqui foi desenvolvido e validado no contexto de uma PoC. Antes de adotar a solução em produção, alguns pontos merecem atenção: 
 Cobertura de cenários : todos os cenários de negócio aplicáveis devem ser testados e validados pelo time funcional e pela área fiscal. 
 Revisão fiscal : a solução como um todo — especialmente os ajustes de parceiro e emissão de NF-e — deve ser revisada por especialistas em tributação brasileira. 
 Clean Core : os exemplos de código apresentados são ilustrativos. Para a solução definitiva, recomenda-se o uso de BRF+ e dos mecanismos de extensibilidade padrão do SAP S/4HANA, evitando lógicas hardcoded e mantendo conformidade com as diretrizes de Clean Core. 
 O Advanced Intercompany Sales tem potencial real para simplificar processos intercompany complexos. A localização para o Brasil exige esses passos adicionais, mas é totalmente viável.  ECC環境では、固定資産取得伝票をFB01で入力し未転記保存した場合、承認者は未転記伝票上で最終的な仕訳内容を確認できていました。 
 Dr 固定資産勘定 
 Cr 現金勘定

 Dr Technical Clearing Account

 伝票1（Operation Part） 
 Dr Technical Clearing Account 
 Cr 現金勘定 
 伝票2（Valuation Part） 
 Dr 固定資産勘定 
 Cr Technical Clearing Account 
 Technical Clearing Account を利用した New Asset Accounting の標準動作であることは認識しております。 

 質問事項 
 ①未転記（Park）時に Operation Part のみ生成され、Valuation Part が生成されない動作は標準仕様でしょうか。

 Keith Fatula, vice president of Solution Engineering at DataXstream, explains the core idea simply. OMS Plus doesn’t have its own database; it’s built directly on SAP Business Technology Platform (SAP BTP) , which means it runs natively inside the SAP ecosystem instead of sitting alongside it.

There’s no separate screen for employees to learn, no swivel-chair workflow between systems, and when SAP rolls out updates, OMS Plus keeps working without any catch-up integration required. 

 The platform is also device agnostic. Whether the user is a call center agent working a phone queue, a field account executive on a tablet, or someone at a front counter, OMS Plus runs the same way across devices without a separate build for each environment. One platform, one interface, one source of truth.

 Fatula is clear about why DataXstream’s AI approach has resonated: the AI lives inside the screen people already use, not in a separate tool they have to switch to.

 His advice to other partners considering SAP Store is direct: don’t just list features. “List out the benefits that your customers are already receiving from your application. Show them the connection—that your application is something they need to look into.” 

 For SAP customers wrestling with order management complexity, DataXstream’s pitch comes down to one idea: the fewer systems you have to stitch together, the fewer things there are to break.
